- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion; if below, add 0.5–1% to avoid underestimation.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.11 to -0.22) triggers downward correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 periods unless confirmed by new data.
